case_data.title: Marialab
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
MariaLab is a Brazilian feminist nonprofit organization founded in 2014 that works at the intersection of gender, technology, and politics. The organization promotes digital security, digital care, and technological autonomy from a feminist and intersectional perspective, addressing inequalities related to gender, sexuality, race, and class.

Through training programmes, digital security support, community infrastructure development, and collective knowledge production, MariaLab works with women, LGBTQIAPN+ communities, human rights defenders, activists, and grassroots organizations across Brazil and Latin America.

Its work is organised around three pillars: Prevention, Support, and Autonomy. Activities include digital security training, risk assessments, emergency support through the Maria d’Ajuda helpline, and the development of autonomous digital infrastructures using free and open-source technologies.
case_data.why-is-this-project-important-to-include:
MariaLab represents a distinctive approach to public engagement in technology governance by working with communities that are often excluded from discussions about AI, digital infrastructures, and technology policy.

Instead of focusing on consultation or deliberation processes, MariaLab builds the long-term capacity of women, LGBTQIAPN+ people, activists, and civil society organizations to understand, question, shape, and govern technological systems that affect their lives.

The project demonstrates how meaningful participation in technology governance requires not only opportunities for engagement but also access to knowledge, digital security, care practices, and technological autonomy. Its feminist and intersectional approach expands conventional understandings of public participation by centering the experiences and expertise of communities disproportionately affected by digital harms and technology-facilitated violence.

Based in Brazil and working across Latin America and the Caribbean, MariaLab brings an important Majority World perspective to debates on technology governance. Through collective learning, digital care practices, community-led infrastructures, and capacity-building initiatives, the organization enables historically marginalized communities to actively participate in shaping technological systems and digital futures. Its work demonstrates that meaningful democratic participation in technology governance requires not only representation, but also access to knowledge, security, resources, and autonomy.
